def M63C2RampExistence {F : RicciFlow n M (Set.Icc a b)} {circumference : ℝ}
    (P : M62.CircleProductData F circumference) : Prop :=
  ∀ gamma : ℝ → P.charts.Point,
    Function.Periodic gamma curvePeriod →
    ContMDiff 𝓘(ℝ, ℝ) (𝓡 (n + 1)) 2 gamma →
    M63IsRampAt P gamma a →
      ∃ c : ℝ → ℝ → P.charts.Point,
        M63C2ShrinkingCurveOn P.flow c (Set.Icc a b) ∧
        (∀ x, c x a = gamma x) ∧
        M63IntrinsicRegularityOn P.flow c (Set.Icc a b) ∧
        ∀ t ∈ Set.Icc a b, M63IsRampAt P (fun x => c x t) t

Proposition
[Global existence for each ramp]

↗ def:ramps-ramp ↗ prop:ramps-length-curvature For each fixed $\rho >0$, every immersed periodic $C^2$ curve with positive slope has a unique $C^2$ pure-normal solution on all of $[a,b]$. Its slope remains positive and its degree is unchanged. Smooth initial labels give the smooth-label branch.
Proof

Start with the local solution. On any compact interval of its existence, the potential $k^2+Q(S,S)$ in (10) is bounded.
